<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via max_length (literal, a string literal in SsoDomainTooLongRefusal; a string literal in tooLong))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-client.mdx`  _(via max_length (literal, a string literal in SsoDomainTooLongRefusal; a string literal in tooLong))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via max_length (literal, a string literal in SsoDomainTooLongRefusal; a string literal in tooLong))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), provider_id (literal, a string literal in findSsoDomainClaim))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via max_length (literal, a string literal in SsoDomainTooLongRefusal; a string literal in tooLong))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via max_length (literal, a string literal in SsoDomainTooLongRefusal; a string literal in tooLong))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via max_length (literal, a string literal in SsoDomainTooLongRefusal; a string literal in tooLong))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via provider_id (literal, a string literal in findSsoDomainClaim))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 45 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aab20c10d7e8762b290a54ea5dc473db94a3eb65` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ae8931fa244f81b9256034c16b2872eeb2d56482` — the merge of head `7a24843d1c860d0af489005126f0cb9f42837f46` into base `aab20c10d7e8762b290a54ea5dc473db94a3eb65`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ae8931fa244f81b9256034c16b2872eeb2d56482 && git checkout ae8931fa244f81b9256034c16b2872eeb2d56482
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin aab20c10d7e8762b290a54ea5dc473db94a3eb65 7a24843d1c860d0af489005126f0cb9f42837f46 && git checkout -B drift-repro aab20c10d7e8762b290a54ea5dc473db94a3eb65 && git merge --no-ff 7a24843d1c860d0af489005126f0cb9f42837f46

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aab20c10d7e8762b290a54ea5dc473db94a3eb65
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs aab20c10d7e8762b290a54ea5dc473db94a3eb65` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `acc38713851b97e61264ef3e1e689b0eb3f4559a`
Local-runs: probe — one `node -e` timing of the new trailing-dot pattern `/\.+$/` on a dot-run string, to tell a polynomial pattern from a linear one before grading F1; nothing built, no test or gate run
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-provider-lifecycle.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-provider-lifecycle.test.ts + (read, not reviewed) packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts, content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx, and the pinned vendor `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 `dist/index.mjs` with `tldts-core` 7.4.16 `extract-hostname.js`

Rendered 2026-11-11T04:33Z. Inputs: card #32308 with every comment through 6787010907, PR #32383 body and file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, register and domain edit: narrowed. Right as a class.** `POST /sso/register` (and the two admin register bridges that reach it) and `POST /sso/update-provider` carrying `domain` now answer `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `field: 'domain'`, for three shapes that saved before: a subdomain that does not win the vendor's whole-value step beside a provider listing its parent; a parent beside a provider that lists the subdomain; one domain in another spelling. Nothing refused on `main` is admitted.
- **Vendor routing as the diff states it: right.** Read in the vendor: `/sign-in/sso` does `findOne` on `domain` equal to the address's domain, then `findMany({ model: "ssoProvider" })` with no `sortBy` and `.find(domainMatches)`; `domainMatches` is "equal, or ends with `.` + entry" over entries parsed by `tldts` `getHostname`, lower-cased. The adapter's `findMany` passes `orderBy` only from `sortBy`. Row order decides step 2, as claimed.
- **Trailing root dot: right.** `tldts` strips it, so a stored `acme.com.` does serve `acme.com` at step 2 and cannot win step 1.
- **Unicode and punycode as one domain: right as a rule, wrong as a description of the vendor** (F5).
- **Wire shape of the refusal: unchanged** (`code`, `status`, `field`, `heldBy` rule); only the message varies by kind. Right, except what the `child` message tells a caller who is not a platform administrator (F2).
- **Public surface: none.** `findSsoDomainClaim` changes signature and `SsoDomainClaim` gains `kind` and `entry`, but neither is imported outside `auth-manager.ts`, and nothing re-exports the module. Right.
- **Shipped edit doors stay open for a stored colliding pair: right.** `edit_saml_provider`, `edit_oidc_provider` and `edit_sso_sign_in_options` send no `domain`, so a certificate or secret rotation on a provider stored colliding before this release is not judged. Only a raw `update-provider` that carries `domain` is.
- **N6 and N7: delivered.** The pin edits a `skip_user_info` OIDC provider through `/admin/sso/update-provider`; the `assertSsoProviderDeletable` comment carries the ruled wording.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, with `!`, the BREAKING banner and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The diff publishes no export, type or schema change, only new refusals on existing routes, and `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The level matches.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — on the PR body and the changeset alike, matching the seat's amendment 6784574779. The declaration is right: each shape was accepted and saved before.

One "before" in the changeset is not true (F4).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (declaration): answered by the seat as the narrowing arm. Agreed, see ②.
- Open question 2 (N3a, two racing registers): answered by the seat, recorded and not fixed. The card's "fix it, or record why not" is met, and the changeset says so to the reader. Agreed.
- Dogfood battery on this head: the dev's reading is `VERDICT command-exit 1` (one 5000 ms timeout in `external-import-walled-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`, green when re-run alone). On CI the `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregate is green with its shards skipped, so no check-run on this head carries a whole-battery green. **Escalated to the seat:** a file re-run alone is not the battery the narrowing arm asks for. The fix for F1 moves the head, so the battery is owed again on the new head in any case; run it without a parallel gate sweep.
- Deviation, tree behind `main` with two derived-family scripts changed there: the queue's to judge at merge, not a contract matter.
- Out-of-scope note, vendor step 2 sees `limit || 100` rows while this check reads every row: left with `carrier: none`. It is the same routing the rule rests on, so it should have a card. **Escalated to the seat** to file.
- Out-of-scope note, a deeper name under a ruled-accepted pair: the module comment now says it. Accepted.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing itself holds.** The published object declares `domain` as "Email domain routed to this IdP", and the vendor declares a comma-separated list for one IdP serving several domains. Neither declares two providers answering for one address domain, and the multi-entry list stays accepted. Each new refusal sits where the vendor's own routing is decided by row order, so the diff makes the existing rule real and takes no declared capability away. The single-entry subdomain beside its parent, ruled accepted, stays accepted both ways round.

Findings:

- **F1, must-fix. `bareDomain` now runs a quadratic pattern on request-controlled input.** `host.replace(/\.+$/, '')` backtracks from every start position of a run of dots that does not end the string. Probe on this box, input `a` + N dots + `x`: N 20000, 312 ms; 40000, 1227 ms; 80000, 4784 ms. `new URL` accepts such a host, and the `catch` branch feeds the same string anyway. `assertSsoProviderDomainFree` calls `providerDomains(ctx.body.domain)` on its first lines, before `resolveActor`, and on `/sso/update-provider` the before-hook reaches it with no earlier refusal of a sessionless caller that I can read; nothing caps the length. One request stalls the auth server's event loop for seconds, and a larger body for minutes. `main` had no pattern here. `register-sso-provider.ts` `bareHostname` is regex-free on purpose for this exact input and names the class (`js/polynomial-redos`). Fix: drop the trailing dots with an index scan and one `slice`, and refuse or ignore an entry longer than a host can be (253) before parsing. Pin it with a long dot-run entry that returns promptly.
- **F2, should-fix. The `child` refusal tells a caller who is not a platform administrator a domain that caller did not name.** With `nameHolder` false the `exact` and `parent` messages say only what the request already held (the requested entry, or a suffix of it). The `child` message names `claim.domain`, the other provider's listed subdomain: an organization administrator who writes `globex.example` on `/sso/update-provider` is told that `eng.globex.example` is an entry of another provider's list. `ssoDomainClaimedRefusal` and the `assertSsoProviderDomainFree` comment both still promise that such a caller "learns only that the domain is served, which `/sign-in/sso` already answers anyone"; `/sign-in/sso` answers that only for a name the caller supplies. Fix: with `nameHolder` false, phrase the `child` refusal on the requested parent alone (a subdomain of it is served by another provider), and pin it beside the existing `another SSO provider` assertion.
- **F3, nit. `winsExactStep` trims; the vendor's step 1 does not.** The vendor stores `body.domain` as typed and step 1 is a plain equality, so a single entry written with surrounding whitespace on the direct `/sso/register` door does not win step 1, yet `value.trim() === entry` reads it as winning and the pair is accepted. It is a residual miss of the N2 class, the grade the review of record gave that class, and admits nothing `main` refused. Since the head moves for F1, compare without the trim there.
- **F4, nit, changeset prose.** "`MÜNCHEN.de` beside a stored `xn--mnchen-3ya.de` … were saved" is not what `main` did: `main` already parsed the request to punycode and narrowed the store by that text, which matches a punycode-stored value, so that leg was refused before. The dev's own ablation A3 goes red only at the punycode-requested, Unicode-stored leg. Name that direction and the trailing dot as the two spellings newly refused.
- **F5, nit, prose.** The changeset gives one reason for all three shapes, "sign-in would not reliably reach the second provider by address". For the Unicode and punycode pair the vendor does not behave that way: `tldts` does not convert to punycode, and the address's domain is not normalised, so each spelling routes only to the provider stored in that spelling. The refusal is right because the two are one DNS domain, not because row order picks. Say so. A consequence worth a follow-up card rather than a fix here: a single-entry subdomain typed in Unicode beside its parent is refused as "another spelling", and the vendor will only ever match a provider stored in Unicode for an address typed in Unicode.
- **F6, nit, PR body.** The body still reads "预期 23 个用例" and takes every reading at `ad29bc9dd8`; the file holds 24 and the head has moved twice.

F1 is a FAIL. F1 and F2 each earn a delta review of their fix. The nits ride the same patch round or become follow-up cards.

Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYm8sWjp2Pk76warN7w` (contract-review subagent)

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7a24843d1c860d0af489005126f0cb9f42837f46`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-provider-lifecycle.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-provider-lifecycle.test.ts + (read, not reviewed) packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts, and the pinned vendor `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 `dist/index.mjs`

Rendered 2026-11-11T08:27Z. Delta review of record 6787108839 (FAIL at `acc38713`). Inputs: card #32308 with every comment through 6790876339, PR #32383 body and file list, the delta `acc38713..7a24843d` on the four PR paths, the net diff against `main` (still those four paths), and the check-runs on this head. The quadratic timing cited below is the probe of the earlier record, not a new run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The judgments of 6787108839 stand** for everything the delta does not touch: the three narrowed shapes, the vendor routing as stated, the unchanged wire shape of the `409`, no public export.
- **New refusal, `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `domain` for length: right.** A value over 255 characters, or an entry over 253 (one trailing root dot not counted), is refused before any parse, for a signed-in caller only. 255 is `sys_sso_provider.domain` `maxLength`; 253 is the host-name limit. It is a further narrowing, and the changeset declares it with its "before".
- **`winsExactStep` by plain equality: right.** The vendor stores `body.domain` as typed and step 1 is an equality. The admin register bridges trim the value before they forward it (`str` in `register-sso-provider.ts`), so only the direct door can store a padded value, and there the strict reading is the true one.
- **The `child` refusal to a caller who is not a platform administrator: right** (F2 below).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, with `!`, the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker, unchanged. The delta adds refusals only; no export, type or schema changes. `Check Changeset` succeeded on this head at 2026-11-11T06:45Z; a second run, started when the PR body was refreshed, was still in progress at this reading, with the changeset file unchanged between the two.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — on the PR body and the changeset alike.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dogfood battery, escalated in 6787108839: answered.** The dev reports one whole run under the lock on this head, `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 451 files passed and 3 skipped, no failure. That is the reading the narrowing arm asks for, on the head this record names. CI's `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregate is green as well.
- **The `limit || 100` note, escalated in 6787108839: answered.** It is card #32388, open.
- The addendum 6790876339 carries no open question and no new out-of-scope finding.
- The F5 consequence (a single-entry subdomain typed in Unicode) is named in the PR body as a candidate follow-up and has no card. Left to the seat; it holds nothing here.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing still holds**, and the delta adds no capability loss: the length cap refuses only values that are not a list of host names.

- **F1, closed.** `withoutTrailingDots` is one backward `charCodeAt` scan and one `slice`; no pattern runs on the value anywhere in the module. In `assertSsoProviderDomainFree` a caller without a session meets a `typeof`, one `trim` and `resolveActor`, then returns: nothing is split or parsed. For a signed-in caller `ssoDomainTooLong` runs before `providerDomains`, and it measures the whole value first, so no `split` runs on a value over 255. Everything parsed after it is at most 255 characters, which bounds every later step whatever its shape: comma runs, whitespace runs and dot runs alike. Stored rows are parsed by the same function, now linear. Pinned: a 300 000-dot value answers `400` at both doors and `401` without a session, a 254-character entry is refused and 253 saved, and the scan has its own timing pin, which the dev's ablation B3 turns red.
- **F2, closed.** With `nameHolder` false the `child` sentence names only `claim.entry`, the parent the request itself holds, and neither the listed subdomain nor the provider. Both comments that state the rule now state it as it is. Pinned for both caller kinds on one request. One residue, accepted: that caller does learn that some subdomain of the name it asked for is served, which `/sign-in/sso` answers only for a name supplied; the comment's "already answers anyone" slightly overstates that. Refusing at all implies it. Nit, no change asked.
- **F3, closed.** `value === entry`, no trim, pinned both ways round.
- **F4 and F5, closed.** Read against `main`: a punycode request beside a Unicode-stored name was saved (the raw narrowing missed it); the reverse leg was already refused, and the changeset now says so; the trailing dot was saved either way round, because `main` kept the dot on whichever side carried it, and the reverse leg has its own pin. The reason for the spelling shape is now "one DNS domain", with the vendor's lack of conversion stated.
- **F6, closed.** The body reads 29 cases and takes every reading at this head.
- **New in the delta:** nothing graded must-fix or should-fix. One nit: an entry is measured as typed, so a scheme or path counts toward the 253; a URL-shaped entry with a valid host can be refused for length. The changeset says so, and the value is not a host name. No change asked.

**VERDICT: PASS**
